headline: Run every planner with a retry; past that, picking a model is an unpriced trade in which each extra point of pass rate costs more, steepest for Atlas-M.
lede: With a retry, {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} passes {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.low.r1.mean} for {cost_per_month.brisk-s.low.r1} a month; {arm:atlas-m.high.r1} passes {compare.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.difference|abs} points more for {cost.gap.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.monthly|abs} more a month. A declared pass-rate floor or price per point would turn this trade into a decision.
flag: Nothing was declared in advance: no control, no floor, no price per point. The planner's owner makes this call, after settling what the monthly volume counts.

caveats.material_if: only once the owner sets a floor or a price per point: that line then picks the option, and the lean below holds only if it lands in the lean's band.

only for gaps whose interval sits near zero: every gap here is read unpaired, which errs wide, so a paired re-read could separate Brisk-S's high reasoning from its low, but would not undo a gap already clear of zero.

only for thin leads, and Atlas-M at high reasoning with a retry is the thin lead it means: the top of {n_candidates|words} configurations, ahead of the lean by an uncorrected interval whose low end is {compare.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.low} points, so its true lead may be smaller or nil. The lean holds either way, since it rests on what each point costs, not on beating Atlas-M.

caveats.label: Cost routing unknown
caveats.material_if: only if another provider serves these models at other prices: no configuration names who served it, so the cost order, every cost multiple between models and every price on the page hold for this run's routing only.

caveats.label: Monthly volume's unit unstated
caveats.material_if: only if the declared {meta.volume_per_month} a month counts tasks rather than calls: then every monthly cost, every price per point and every band in the explore rows grows by the configurations' calls per task, between {measure.calls_per_task.atlas-m.high.r1.mean} and {measure.calls_per_task.nano-xs.off.r1.mean} on the frontier, and an owner pricing a point against today's bands could land in the wrong one. The owner should settle the unit before pricing.

decision.text: Cost against pass rate. The cheapest configuration, {arm:nano-xs.off.r0}, passes {measure.pass_rate.nano-xs.off.r0.mean} for {cost_per_month.nano-xs.off.r0} a month; the highest, {arm:atlas-m.high.r1}, passes {measure.pass_rate.atlas-m.high.r1.mean} for {cost_per_month.atlas-m.high.r1}. Every option between them on the frontier runs with a retry.

Each step up the frontier costs more per point a month: {price.nano-xs.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} from {arm:nano-xs.high.r1} to {arm:brisk-s.low.r1}, {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} on to {arm:brisk-s.high.r1}, and {price.brisk-s.high.r1.atlas-m.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} on to {arm:atlas-m.high.r1}. These prices are point estimates; the last two steps buy gains this run cannot tell from zero. Every band is listed under What you could change.

Ours, not a declared rule: {arm:brisk-s.low.r1}, for a point worth between {price.nano-xs.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} and {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} a month. It is clearly ahead of {arm:nano-xs.high.r1} (interval {compare.brisk-s.low.r1.nano-xs.high.r1.pass_rate.overall.interval} points), and the next step up buys a gain not separated from zero.

{arm:atlas-m.high.r1} is ahead of the lean, with an interval of {compare.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.interval} points that clears zero only narrowly, read unpaired and uncorrected across {n_candidates|words} configurations, at {cost.gap.atlas-m.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.multiple} its cost at this run's unnamed routing. No margin or floor was declared, so no option sits near a line.

A declaration first: the owner settles what the monthly volume counts, then sets a pass-rate floor or a price per point. Then a re-run of Brisk-S at high against low reasoning, both with a retry, at {settle.brisk-s.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.cases_needed_80} cases each (the size for independent arms; fewer if paired on the same cases), tells them apart four times in five.

claims.text: Cost and pass rate trade along one frontier: from {arm:nano-xs.off.r0} to {arm:atlas-m.high.r1}, cost per thousand calls rises {cost.gap.atlas-m.high.r1.nano-xs.off.r0.multiple} at this run's unnamed routing, and {count.frontier.pass_rate|words} configurations sit on it.

evidence.caption: Cost per thousand calls, on a log scale, against pass rate for every configuration, at this run's unnamed provider routing; the table below names the frontier's configurations.
The frontier configurations in order, each step with its price per point of pass rate a month; point estimates at the declared volume.

claims.text: A retry lifts pass rate for every model, most where the model is weakest: {lever.retry.nano-xs.off.r0.nano-xs.off.r1.pass_rate.effect} points for {arm:nano-xs.off.r0}, against {lever.retry.atlas-m.high.r0.atlas-m.high.r1.pass_rate.effect} for {arm:atlas-m.high.r0}, the only pairing whose interval reaches zero. At this run's unnamed routing it adds at most {cost.gap.atlas-m.high.r1.atlas-m.high.r0.per_1k|abs} per thousand calls.

evidence.caption: Pass-rate gain from adding a retry, in points, with unpaired intervals, for one configuration per model.
The same gain for another configuration per model; the remaining pairings' rates, without intervals, are in Every arm by measure.

claims.text: At the top, neither the bigger model nor more reasoning is told apart on its own: with a retry, Brisk-S trails Atlas-M by {lever.model.atlas-m.low.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.effect|abs} points at low reasoning, and high reasoning adds {lever.reasoning.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.effect} for Brisk-S; both intervals cross zero. At this run's unnamed routing, Atlas-M costs {cost.gap.atlas-m.low.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.multiple} as much at the same settings.

evidence.caption: Effect of switching model or raising reasoning among the retry configurations of Atlas-M and Brisk-S, in points, with unpaired intervals.

claims.text: Model and reasoning set the median latency; the retry leaves the median unchanged in every pair shown and lengthens the slow tail, {arm:brisk-s.low.r1} reading {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r1.p95} at p95 against {measure.latency_ms.brisk-s.low.r0.p95} without it. No latency budget was declared.

evidence.caption: Latency from median to p95 for every frontier configuration beside its twin with or without a retry.

claims.text: Multi-hop questions are the weakest task for each of the three frontier options shown; the lean passes {task.multihop.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean} there against {task.single.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.mean} on single lookups.

evidence.caption: Pass rate by task; the snapshot states no case count per task, so these rows carry no interval and are descriptive.

claims.text: The lean's kept failures each break differently: a multi-hop question collapsed into one search, a date window off by a day, and an ambiguous name searched instead of asked about. The snapshot does not say how many failures they were kept from.

evidence.caption: Every failure the snapshot keeps for the lean, one per task where kept; a sample, not a count.

explore.control: What a point of pass rate is worth a month
explore.outcome: Below {price.nano-xs.off.r0.nano-xs.off.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} a point, {arm:nano-xs.off.r0}; {price.nano-xs.off.r0.nano-xs.off.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} to {price.nano-xs.off.r1.nano-xs.low.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point}, {arm:nano-xs.off.r1}; {price.nano-xs.off.r1.nano-xs.low.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} to {price.nano-xs.low.r1.nano-xs.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point}, {arm:nano-xs.low.r1}; {price.nano-xs.low.r1.nano-xs.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} to {price.nano-xs.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point}, {arm:nano-xs.high.r1}; {price.nano-xs.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} to {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point}, {arm:brisk-s.low.r1}; {price.brisk-s.low.r1.brisk-s.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point} to {price.brisk-s.high.r1.atlas-m.high.r1.pass_rate.monthly_per_point}, {arm:brisk-s.high.r1}; above that, {arm:atlas-m.high.r1}. Point estimates, read with the volume as calls; if it counts tasks, every band grows by the calls per task.

explore.binds: The cheapest configuration that meets it
explore.outcome: Read on point estimates: a floor up to {measure.pass_rate.nano-xs.high.r1.mean} keeps a Nano-XS configuration; up to {measure.pass_rate.brisk-s.high.r1.mean}, a Brisk-S one; above that, only {arm:atlas-m.high.r1}.

omitted.what: No-retry configurations other than the cheapest
omitted.why: Each passes less often than its own retry twin, which costs a little more; the retry claim shows the gain, and their rates are in Every arm by measure.
Varies little across configurations and decides nothing; it enters only the volume caveat.
The snapshot lists them but holds no figures for either.

omitted.what: Model and reasoning effects without a retry, and their interactions
omitted.why: Off the frontier; they don't change which options a decider would weigh. Each arm's rates are in Every arm by measure; the effects' intervals are not on the page.
No case counts per task, so no interval; descriptive only and the order matches overall.

next.text: The planner's owner settles what the monthly volume counts, then declares a pass-rate floor or a price per point of pass rate.

next.settles: Whether high reasoning's gain over the lean is real, which a run of today's size reads the wrong way {settle.brisk-s.high.r1.brisk-s.low.r1.pass_rate.overall.wrong_side} of the time.

method.text: Each of the {n_candidates|words} configurations ran {scoreboard.brisk-s.low.r1.cases} cases with no lost or failed trials; repeats are not stated. Configurations cross {count.levels.model|words} models, {count.levels.reasoning|words} reasoning levels, and a retry or none.

The pipeline's pass or fail grade on each planned query. Failures are classed as a missing call, wrong arguments, the wrong tool or malformed output; the snapshot defines pass no further. On ambiguous entities the expected answer is a clarifying question.

Read at {lever.retry.nano-xs.off.r0.nano-xs.off.r1.pass_rate.level} from each configuration's binomial spread over its cases and combined as if the configurations ran different cases, which errs wide; uncorrected for the number of comparisons. Per-task figures carry none.
Cost per thousand calls as measured, at a provider routing no configuration names. Monthly figures use the declared {meta.volume_per_month} a month, whose unit the campaign does not state.
Median and p95 per configuration; no budget was declared.
No control and no criteria were declared, so no option is read against a line.
